practiceQuestions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India vide the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, which paved the way for a comprehensive dual GST system. [Primary Reference: Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 / Official UPSC GS-3 Economy Syllabus]

practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) established?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 279A of the Constitution of India empowers the President to constitute a GST Council, making it a federal constitutional body designed to deliberate on GST rates, exemptions, and thresholds. [Primary Reference: Article 279A, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who is the Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council?
opts: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
practiceQuestions.sol: As per Article 279A, the Union Finance Minister acts as the Chairperson of the GST Council, while the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance is a member. [Primary Reference: Article 279A(2), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: GST is a destination-based tax. What does 'destination-based' imply regarding its taxation principle?
opts: Tax is collected where the goods or services are manufactured or produced.
Tax is collected by the Central Government alone.
Tax is accrued to the state where the goods or services are ultimately consumed.
Tax is levied strictly on international exports.
practiceQuestions.sol: GST is a destination-based consumption tax, meaning the revenue from the tax goes to the consuming state rather than the state where the product is manufactured. [Primary Reference: Economic Survey / Union Budget Documents]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following taxes was NOT subsumed into the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Basic Customs Duty (BCD) on imports is kept outside the purview of GST and continues to be levied separately under the Customs Act, 1962. [Primary Reference: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the voting weight of the Central Government and the State Governments combined within the GST Council?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 279A, the vote of the Central Government has a weightage of one-third (33.33%) of the total votes cast, and the votes of all the State Governments combined have a weightage of two-thirds (66.67%). [Primary Reference: Article 279A(9), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which body acts as the IT backbone for implementing the Goods and Services Tax in India?
opts: Reserve Bank Information Technology Private Limited (ReBIT)
practiceQuestions.sol: GSTN (Goods and Services Tax Network) is a non-profit, non-government company that provides shared IT infrastructure and services to the Central and State governments, taxpayers, and other stakeholders. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Finance, Government Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: What fraction of total weighted votes is required for any decision of the GST Council to be validly passed?
opts: Not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of members present and voting
practiceQuestions.sol: Every decision of the GST Council is taken at a meeting by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting. [Primary Reference: Article 279A(10), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following falls under the category of 'Zero-Rated Supply' under the GST regime?
opts: Supply of goods and services to educational institutions
Exports of goods or services and supplies to SEZs
Supply of agricultural produce directly from farmers
Exempted goods notified by the GST Council
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 16 of the IGST Act, exports of goods and services and supplies to Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are treated as 'zero-rated supplies', meaning no tax is levied on the export itself, and input tax credit is refundable. [Primary Reference: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of the Goods and Services Tax Compensation Cess levied on certain luxury and demerit goods?
opts: To fund universal basic income schemes
To compensate states for any revenue loss arising from the implementation of GST
To subsidize agricultural fertilizers and seeds
practiceQuestions.sol: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 established a compensation cess to provide financial compensation to states for loss of revenue resulting from the introduction of GST for a transition period. [Primary Reference: Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Input Tax Credit (ITC) mechanism eliminate the cascading effect of taxes under the GST framework?
opts: By exempting raw materials from all forms of indirect taxation at origin.
By allowing businesses to claim credit for taxes paid on inputs at each stage of value addition against the final tax liability.
By transferring tax collection responsibility entirely to the final consumer.
By levying a single unified tax directly at the manufacturing level.
practiceQuestions.sol: ITC allows businesses to deduct the tax they paid on raw materials and business inputs (GST paid on purchase) from the tax they collect on outward supplies (GST collected on sales), ensuring tax is paid only on the incremental value addition, thus eliminating tax-on-tax (cascading effect). [Primary Reference: CGST Act, 2017 / Economic Survey]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the structural distinction between CGST, SGST/UTGST, and IGST in terms of applicability?
opts: CGST and SGST apply to interstate trade, while IGST applies to intrastate trade.
CGST and SGST/UTGST apply to intrastate supplies, while IGST applies to interstate supplies and imports.
IGST is collected by states, whereas CGST and SGST are collected exclusively by the Centre.
There is no difference; all three are interchangeable terms for the same tax levy.
practiceQuestions.sol: In an intrastate transaction, tax is split equally between Central GST (CGST) and State/UT GST (SGST/UTGST). In an interstate transaction or import, Integrated GST (IGST) is levied by the Centre and subsequently apportioned to the consuming state. [Primary Reference: Article 246A, Constitution of India / IGST Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the inclusion of petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) under Article 279A operate currently?
opts: They are fully subsumed under standard GST slabs.
They are constitutionally part of GST, but the GST Council has decided a zero tax rate for them.
They are included in GST, but taxed at a flat rate of 28% without exceptions.
They are constitutionally part of GST, but goods and services tax will be levied on them from a date recommended by the GST Council.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 279A(5) states that the GST Council shall recommend the date on which goods and services tax be levied on petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, motor spirit, natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel. Currently, they continue to attract legacy central and state taxes. [Primary Reference: Article 279A(5), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What constitutional mechanism was introduced by the 101st Amendment Act to empower both Parliament and State Legislatures to simultaneously levy GST?
opts: Concurrent List expansion under Seventh Schedule
Insertion of Article 246A conferring simultaneous power
Transfer of all taxation powers exclusively to the Union List
Creation of an independent financial judiciary
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 246A was inserted by the 101st Amendment Act, granting Parliament and the Legislature of every State the power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax imposed by the Union or by such State, establishing a unique concurrent taxation space. [Primary Reference: Article 246A, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the GST Council considered a unique experiment in cooperative federalism in India?
opts: Because it gives the Centre absolute veto power over all state fiscal policies.
Because it institutionalizes joint decision-making where both Union and States vote on tax rates and laws on a shared platform.
Because states independently decide tax rates without Union interference.
Because all revenue collected is retained entirely by the states.
practiceQuestions.sol: The GST Council embodies cooperative federalism as it brings the Union and all States/UTs together on a constitutional platform to jointly decide indirect tax policies, rates, and exemptions, balancing federal fiscal supremacy with regional autonomy. [Primary Reference: Supreme Court Judgment in Union of India v. Mohit Mineral Pvt. Ltd., 2022]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the legal status and binding nature of the recommendations made by the GST Council?
opts: They are strictly binding executive orders that take effect without legislative action.
They are purely advisory and non-binding on both Parliament and State Legislatures.
They are recommendations upon which Parliament and State Legislatures enact laws, reflecting cooperative federal dialogue rather than pure executive diktat.
They are binding on states but completely optional for the Central Government.
practiceQuestions.sol: As clarified by the Supreme Court in the Mohit Minerals case (2022), recommendations of the GST Council are collaborative inputs. While Parliament and State legislatures enact laws based on them, they are not unbending executive orders, though cooperative federalism requires broad adherence to maintain a unified national market. [Primary Reference: Supreme Court of India - Union of India v. Mohit Mineral Pvt. Ltd., 2022]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the 'Anti-Profiteering' measure under the GST law function?
opts: It prevents companies from setting prices above a maximum retail price fixed by the Prime Minister.
It ensures that reduction in tax rates or the benefit of input tax credit is passed on to consumers by way of commensurate reduction in prices.
It taxes corporate profits at 100% if they exceed targeted annual revenue.
It penalizes entities that export goods without paying basic customs duty.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 171 of the CGST Act mandates that any reduction in rate of tax on any supply of goods or services or the benefit of input tax credit shall be passed on to the recipient by way of commensurate reduction in prices, monitored by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) / National Anti-profiteering Authority (NAA). [Primary Reference: Section 171, CGST Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the E-Way Bill system integrated with the GST framework?
opts: It replaces paper currency with digital wallet transactions for all retail buyers.
It is an electronic document generated for the movement of goods exceeding a specified valuation across state or intrastate borders, ensuring compliance and tracking tax evasion.
It serves as an international shipping permit issued by the World Trade Organization.
It is a mandatory permit required to transport agricultural seeds between villages.
practiceQuestions.sol: An E-Way Bill is an electronic compliance document mandated under GST rules for the movement of goods of consignment value exceeding Rs. 50,000, curbing tax evasion by tracking physical transit in real-time. [Primary Reference: Rule 138, CGST Rules, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the GST framework address 'composite supply' and 'mixed supply' differently?
opts: Composite supplies are taxed at the highest rate among all items, whereas mixed supplies are taxed at the lowest rate.

In a composite supply, items are naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business and taxed at the rate of the principal supply; in a mixed supply, items are artificially bundled and taxed at the rate of the item attracting the highest tax rate.
Composite supplies are exempt from GST, while mixed supplies attract a flat 28% IGST.
There is no legal distinction between the two under the CGST Act.
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 8 of the CGST Act differentiates them: a composite supply (naturally bundled, like a hotel stay with breakfast) takes the tax rate of the principal supply, while a mixed supply (artificially bundled, like a gift hamper of chocolates and wine) is taxed at the rate of the single item attracting the highest tax rate. [Primary Reference: Sections 2(30), 2(74) & 8, CGST Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary rationale behind setting up the Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT)?
opts: To adjudicate disputes and appeals arising under the CGST and SGST/IGST Acts, providing a specialized judicial forum and reducing the burden on High Courts.
To directly audit corporate balance sheets for tax evasion without notifying the Finance Ministry.
To fix national tax rates and GST slabs without convening the GST Council.
To act as an international arbitration tribunal for cross-border e-commerce disputes.
practiceQuestions.sol: GSTAT serves as the specialized second-stage appellate forum under the GST laws to resolve tax disputes between taxpayers and tax authorities, ensuring uniformity in adjudication and decreasing litigation backlogs in writ courts. [Primary Reference: Finance Act / CGST Act Amendments relating to GSTAT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council):
1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 279A of the Constitution of India.
2. The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of the GST Council.
3. Every decision of the GST Council must be approved by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 279A provides for the creation of the GST Council. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson, not the Prime Minister. Statement 3 is correct: Article 279A(10) stipulates the three-fourths weighted votes majority requirement. [Primary Reference: Article 279A, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the voting structure in the GST Council:
1. The vote of the Central Government has a weightage of one-third of total votes cast.
2. The votes of all State Governments combined have a weightage of two-thirds of total votes cast.
3. A state can unilaterally veto any proposal in the GST Council regardless of the weighted voting tally.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per Article 279A(9): Centre holds 33.33% and states collectively hold 66.67% voting weight. Statement 3 is incorrect because decisions require a 75% majority of members present and voting; no single state possesses an individual veto power. [Primary Reference: Article 279A(9) & (10), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the taxation of petroleum products under the GST regime:
1. Petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, petrol, natural gas, and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) are permanently excluded from the GST framework by the Constitution.
2. The GST Council is empowered to recommend the date from which GST will be levied on these petroleum products.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: They are not 'permanently' excluded; rather, they are constitutionally part of GST but kept in abeyance. Statement 2 is correct: Article 279A(5) mandates that the GST Council shall recommend the date on which levy of GST on these items will commence. [Primary Reference: Article 279A(5), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN):
1. GSTN is incorporated as a fully government-owned public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Finance.
2. It provides the front-end and back-end IT infrastructure for registration, return filing, and tax payment processing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: GSTN was originally set up as a Section 8 (not-for-profit) private limited company with equity participation from private financial institutions, though subsequently converted into a 100% government-owned company. However, it was not a traditional PSU. Statement 2 is correct: GSTN provides the robust IT backbone for return filing, registration, and tax administration. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Finance / GSTN Corporate Structure Reports]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Input Tax Credit (ITC) under GST:
1. ITC allows a registered person to reduce the tax paid on business inputs from the tax payable on outward supplies.
2. ITC can be claimed on goods or services used for personal consumption as long as the taxpayer is registered under GST.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: ITC forms the core mechanism to prevent cascading taxes by crediting taxes paid on inputs. Statement 2 is incorrect: Section 17(5) of the CGST Act explicitly blocks ITC on goods and services used for personal consumption or non-business purposes. [Primary Reference: Sections 16 & 17(5), CGST Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Zero-Rated Supply' under GST:
1. Zero-rated supply means the goods and services exported attract a zero percent tax rate, but input tax credit cannot be refunded.
2. Exports of goods and services and supplies to Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are treated as zero-rated supplies under the IGST Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Under zero-rated supply, input tax credit is fully refundable or accumulated tax paid on inputs can be refunded, unlike exempt supplies where ITC lapses. Statement 2 is correct: Section 16 of the IGST Act defines exports and SEZ supplies as zero-rated. [Primary Reference: Section 16, IGST Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the GST Compensation Cess:
1. It is levied on luxury and demerit goods to provide compensation to states for revenue loss arising from GST implementation.
2. The revenue collected from the compensation cess is pooled into the Consolidated Fund of India and cannot be kept in a public account.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Compensation Cess is levied under the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017 to bridge state revenue deficits during the transition. Statement 2 is incorrect: The proceeds are credited to a non-lapsable fund known as the GST Compensation Fund, which forms part of the Public Account of India, not the Consolidated Fund of India. [Primary Reference: Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Anti-Profiteering' provisions under GST:
1. The provisions aim to ensure that businesses pass on the benefits of reduced tax rates or input tax credits to consumers through lower prices.
2. Complaints of profiteering can be investigated by anti-profiteering institutional mechanisms, and penalties can include cancellation of registration or refund with interest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 171 of the CGST Act sets up the anti-profiteering mandate to protect consumers from unjustified price hikes post-GST rate cuts, empowering authorities to order price reductions, refunds to consumers, or penalties including registration cancellation. [Primary Reference: Section 171, CGST Act, 2017 / CGST Rules]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the E-Way Bill mechanism:
1. It is a physical paper permit that must be stamped by local excise officers before any goods can leave a factory gate.
2. It is generated electronically on the common portal for the movement of goods whose consignment value exceeds fifty thousand rupees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: E-Way Bills are electronic documents generated online, not physical stamped paper permits. Statement 2 is correct: Rule 138 of CGST Rules mandates E-Way bill generation on the GST portal for consignments exceeding Rs. 50,000. [Primary Reference: Rule 138, CGST Rules, 2017]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Composite Supply' and 'Mixed Supply' under GST:
1. A composite supply comprises two or more taxable supplies of goods or services naturally bundled and supplied in the ordinary course of business, taxed at the rate of the principal supply.
2. A mixed supply comprises two or more individual supplies made together for a single price where the items are artificially bundled, and it is taxed at the rate of the item that attracts the highest rate of tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 2(30) read with Section 8 defines composite supply (naturally bundled, principal tax rate applies), while Section 2(74) read with Section 8 defines mixed supply (artificially bundled, highest tax rate applies). [Primary Reference: Sections 2(30), 2(74) & 8, CGST Act, 2017]
